name: Sustainable growth rate (SGR)
title: Sustainable Growth Rate: ROE, Retention & Assumptions
description: Understand the annual ROE × retention approximation, a worked 9% example, financing assumptions and the difference from actual growth.
definition: Sustainable growth rate is modeled here as annual return on equity multiplied by the share of earnings retained, under stated stable operating and capital-policy assumptions.
explanation: Retention is one minus the dividend payout ratio for matching positive annual income. The product is a conditional approximation, not a revenue-growth forecast. Its financing interpretation keeps the capital structure stable without new equity issuance, while debt can increase proportionally. A no-external-financing internal-growth model is a separate task.
formula: Annual SGR = annual ROE × (1 − dividend payout ratio).
formulaNote: Use matching annual factors. The accounting worksheet uses a two-point average of positive beginning and ending book equity. Other denominator and timing conventions need reconciliation.

example.title: A 40% payout leaves 60% of earnings
example.answer: The stated annual ROE × retention model gives 9%. It does not predict next year’s sales.
example.assumptions: An annual ROE × retention approximation for positive ROE, positive earnings/equity in accounting mode, and dividend payout from 0% to 100%. Fixed policy assumptions, no full financing model, new equity issuance, market feed, growth forecast or automatic valuation growth input.

pitfall.title: Sustainable growth is not a guarantee of actual growth
pitfall.text: The 9% product for 15% ROE and 60% retention does not establish that sales will grow 9%, that cash is available, or that a lender will fund the implied borrowing. It also is not automatically a valid perpetual valuation growth input.

tools.text: Inspect the annual ratio, accounting bridge and target-retention scenarios.
Reconcile the supplied income and book-equity scope separately.
